Definition: to tie fast; hence (of the mouth) to be tongue-tied
BiblicalUsage: The word binds a mouth shut. Joseph's sheaf stands upright while his brothers' sheaves bow, and the binding is in the dream, sheaves tied fast together. Isaiah uses the same root for the Suffering Servant, who is brought as a lamb to the slaughter and as a sheep before her shearers is dumb, so He openeth not His mouth.
TheologicalSignificance: A word for a tied tongue carries no doctrine of its own; its weight is the Servant's silence, that the one who could have spoken chose not to, and His silence was part of the offering.
